They list three **Must Fix** items before the PR can be accepted. There are no inline comments and no formal review. No checks have run, and GitHub now says the PR has **merge conflicts** (it was mergeable yesterday).

Their line numbers point at the PR head (`6270fbc`). Main has two newer commits in `confirm-phone`, so some lines have moved. I looked at the code each item cites:

1. **Only send the API key to approved servers.** Right now `CALLE_API_BASE` is read from the environment and used as-is ([calle.ts:198](supabase/functions/_shared/calle.ts:198)). Both POSTs to `/v1/calls` send `Bearer ${calleApiKey}` to whatever that address is, and they follow redirects by default. The fix: accept only a fixed list of HTTPS addresses, and set `redirect: "error"` (or `"manual"`) on those requests. Fake transports injected in tests can stay.

2. **Don't claim no call was placed when we can't know.**
   - [calle.ts:~578](supabase/functions/_shared/calle.ts) logs `"no call was placed"` whenever there's no call ID.
   - The dispatch-failure path writes `disposition: "not_answered", billable: false` ([calle.ts:~259–276](supabase/functions/_shared/calle.ts)). That is a claim that nothing was charged.
   - [confirm-phone/index.ts:88](supabase/functions/confirm-phone/index.ts:88) tells the user "Try again in a few minutes."

   They want wording like "unknown, needs manual review" instead, and no prompt to start a fresh confirmation. They say explicitly that the reconciliation logic doesn't need a redesign.

3. **Hide phone numbers in what the UI shows, and narrow a README claim.**
   - Numbers in history, summaries and previews should be masked on screen, while the stored private record keeps them ([history/model.ts:35](web/src/routes/app/history/model.ts:35), `dispatch-mode.ts:454–471`).
   - The README's halt section ([README.md:323](README.md:323)) should say it stops *future* calls, not that it cancels calls CALL-E has already accepted.

All three are small, contained changes. Items 2 and 3 are mostly wording and display masking. Item 1 is the only real code change.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package Orma into a checkout of CALLE-AI/awesome-phone-call-agents.
#
# Usage: scripts/package-list-pr.sh <list-repo-checkout>
#
# The copy comes from the committed HEAD, never the working tree. It lands in
# apps/web/orma/ and leaves out proxy/, dev-diary/, design/ and agent files.
# The script then scans the copy, runs the tests inside it, adds the index row,
# and runs the list repository's own validator. Any failure stops the run.

set -euo pipefail

target="${1:-}"
if [ -z "$target" ] || [ ! -f "$target/scripts/validate_repository.py" ] || [ ! -d "$target/apps" ]; then
  echo "usage: scripts/package-list-pr.sh <checkout of awesome-phone-call-agents>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

src="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
target="$(cd "$target" && pwd)"
dest="$target/apps/web/orma"

fail() {
  echo "package-list-pr: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

echo "package-list-pr: copying HEAD $(git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD) into apps/web/orma"
rm -rf "$dest"
mkdir -p "$dest"
git -C "$src" archive --format=tar HEAD \
  web supabase scripts testdata docs .env.example README.md \
  | tar -x -C "$dest"
rm -f "$dest/scripts/package-list-pr.sh"

# The copy has no proxy Worker, so its README says what stands in for it.
python3 - "$dest/README.md" <<'PY'
import sys
path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
note = """## About this copy

This directory packages Orma for the CALL-E awesome list. It includes the web app, the Supabase schema and functions, the local stack script and the recorded fixtures.

It leaves out the `proxy/` Worker. That Worker is a plain pass-through to the Supabase project. The web app and the functions refuse any API URL containing `supabase.co`, so a self-hosted deployment needs its own reverse proxy in front of the project. Point `ORMA_API_URL` at that proxy.

The local walkthrough below needs no proxy and places no calls.

"""
marker = "## What Orma is"
if marker not in text:
    sys.exit("README has no 'What Orma is' section to anchor the note")
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(marker, note + marker, 1))
PY

echo "package-list-pr: scanning the copy"
secret_patterns='sb_secret_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|re_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|[0-9]{8,10}:AA[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}|"private_key"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"-----BEGIN'
if hits="$(grep -rlIE "$secret_patterns" "$dest" 2>/dev/null)"; then
  fail "key-shaped text in: ${hits//$dest\//}"
fi
# A PEM header alone is code that parses keys. Key material follows the header.
if hits="$(grep -rlIPz -- '-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----(\\n|\n)[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}' "$dest" 2>/dev/null)"; then
  fail "private key material in: ${hits//$dest\//}"
fi

found_env="$(find "$dest" -name '.env' -o -name '.env.*' ! -name '.env.example' | head -1)"
[ -z "$found_env" ] || fail "an env file was copied: ${found_env#$dest/}"

big="$(find "$dest" -type f -size +5M | head -1)"
[ -z "$big" ] || fail "file over 5 MB: ${big#$dest/}"

if [ -f "$src/.env" ]; then
  owner_digits="$(grep -E '^ORMA_OWNER_PHONE=' "$src/.env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -cd '0-9')"

echo "package-list-pr: running Deno tests in the copy"

    [ -f "supabase/functions/_shared/${suite}_tests.ts" ] && files="$files supabase/functions/_shared/${suite}_tests.ts"

files="$(find "$dest" -type f | wc -l)"
size="$(du -sh "$dest" | cut -f1)"
echo "package-list-pr: done. $files files, $size, in apps/web/orma"

## Cancellation

Users and operators have full control over stopping calls and removing data.

### User cancellation (Settings page)

Users can manage or stop calls from `https://orma.nryn.dev/app/settings`:
- **Cancel today's call**: Moves a still `scheduled` run to `canceled`, so it never rings. Today also offers "Cancel this call". Later calls stay scheduled.
- **Pause all calls**: Marks every saved call time inactive. The materialiser then removes future runs from inactive times.
- **Turn calls off**: Sets `revoked_at` on the user's `outbound_calls` consent row. The dispatcher refuses every run for a profile without live consent.
- **Delete account**: Calls `delete_my_account`. It deletes the user's voice notes from the `item-audio` bucket, then deletes the auth user, which cascades through the user's rows.

### Operator cancellation

An operator can halt all platform calls and recurring jobs directly:

1. Unschedule the cron jobs in SQL:

```sql
select cron.unschedule('tick-runs');
select cron.unschedule('materialise-runs');
select cron.unschedule('analysis-report');
```

2. Re-enable dry-run mode in Supabase secrets so no real calls go out:

```bash
supabase secrets set ORMA_DRY_RUN=true
```

## Dry run

Orma enforces dry run mode by default. Developers opt into spending, never out of it.

`ORMA_DRY_RUN` defaults to `true`. Only the exact value `false` turns it off. While dry run is on, the dispatcher never contacts the CALL-E API and places no actual calls.

Use `ORMA_DRY_RUN_FIXTURE` to select the simulated outcome:
- `completed` (default): Simulates an answered call with valid extraction.
- `failed`: Simulates an unanswered call.
- `no_result`: Simulates an answered call where result validation fails.

A dry run marks the run `billable = false` with `terminal_writer = 'dry_run'`. It writes three `call_events` rows:
- `dispatched`: `dispatch_mode` `dry_run`, `fixture`, `outbound_request_made: false`, the masked `request_body`, and `request_body_masked: true`.
- `ingested`: Written by `ingest_call_result`, the same as for a live call. It carries `call_run_id`, `calle_call_id`, `state`, `disposition`, `item_count`, `mention_count`, `retirement_count`, `commitment_count` and `skipped`.
- `finalised`: `dispatch_mode`, `fixture`, `outbound_request_made: false`, `state`, `disposition`, `item_count`, `mention_count` and `failure_reason`.

## Summary

Orma is a daily two-minute accountability call. It rings at a time you chose, leads with what you keep not doing, asks what needs capturing, and lets you drop an item without argument.

The call arrives already knowing. SQL counts mentions and ages, and those numbers are rendered into the CALL-E task before dispatch, so the model phrases facts it never computed: "You've mentioned the dentist 3 times. It's been 34 days." A structured result schema writes captured items, retirements with transcript evidence offsets, and commitments back to Postgres.

Orma owns the scheduler, following this repository's provider-separation principle. `pg_cron` materialises runs, a minute tick claims them with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and dispatches with a stable idempotency key, and results come back through a re-fetched webhook and polling.

Surfaces: a SvelteKit web app for setup and review, a Telegram bot for text and voice capture and receipts, and an MCP server with six tools under the user's own JWT and row-level security.

The app lives in `apps/web/orma/` with its own README. It also adds one row to `apps/README.md`.

- [x] Real-world side effects are clearly described. The README has a side-effects table covering calls, the three cron jobs, the confirmation call, Telegram messages, pattern report email, and stored voice notes.
- [x] Phone numbers are masked in documentation and test fixtures unless they are clearly fictional.
- [x] Recurring workflows include cancellation behavior. Users can cancel today's call, pause all calls, revoke consent, or delete the account. Operators can unschedule each cron job and turn dry run back on.
- [x] Runnable code has a dry-run, fake-server, or no-call path by default. `ORMA_DRY_RUN` defaults to true and fails closed when unset.

## Safety

- **Explicit intent.** No call is placed without a consent row that stores the exact wording shown, a slot the user chose, and a confirmed number.
- **Authorized destinations.** Anyone can sign up, so a typed number is not trusted. A one-time call reads a six-digit code, and the user enters it in the app. Only then does the server set the confirmed flag. Users cannot set it themselves, and changing the number clears it. Attempts are rate limited and never redialled.

The fixes from #707 are live in production. Nothing errored and nothing changed in production secrets or settings.

**What went out:**
- **Edge Functions:** `confirm-phone`, `calle-webhook` and `tick`. These are the only ones that import the changed code.
- **Web app:** new version `bbe2ce3a`, which masks phone numbers on the History and Today pages.
- **Before deploying**, I checked that the production `CALLE_API_BASE` secret is exactly `https://api.heycall-e.com`, by matching its SHA-256 digest. The new check makes every function refuse to start if that value is anything else.

**Checks after the deploy:**
- `confirm-phone` answers the browser's preflight request (204).
- `calle-webhook` rejects a request with a wrong secret (405). Both would have failed with a 5xx if the address check blocked startup.
- `tick` runs every minute from its schedule, and those runs return 200. The Supabase logs from 05:20 to 05:38 UTC show normal starts and no errors or warnings.
- Signed out, `/` and `/login` return 200, and `/app` and `/app/history` redirect to `/login`.
- I haven't signed in to look at the masked History page, or placed a live call to test the new "outcome unknown" wording.

My first probe also sent a POST to `tick` in production. The auto-mode check blocked it; running `tick` by hand could dispatch real calls. I used safe requests and the logs instead.

I recorded the deploy in the memory graph. The CI check on #707 is still waiting for a CALLE-AI maintainer to approve it.

The keepalive job has never run. Its GitHub workflow has zero runs. The repo is also missing the SUPABASE_POOLER_URL and BACKUP_REPO_TOKEN secrets and the BACKUP_REPO variable. The phase doc marked this task done, but it isn't. A free Supabase project pauses after 7 days of low activity, which could take the demo down during judging (30 Sep – 13 Oct).
I'll look at the workflow, its run history, what secrets and variables the repo actually has, and what the phase doc claims, before changing anything.

- **It never ran.** The workflow reached `main` on 14 Sep at 14:52 UTC. The only scheduled run due since then was today at 03:17 UTC, and GitHub didn't run it; GitHub often skips the first scheduled runs of a new workflow.

name: Keepalive

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: keepalive
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # A free Supabase project pauses after seven days of low activity. One
  # PostgREST read a day keeps it active. It needs no secrets.
  #
  # It calls the project host, not ORMA_API_URL. The Cloudflare front door
  # challenges GitHub's datacenter addresses and answered 403 on the first run.
  # The front door exists for the operator's network, which misresolves
  # *.supabase.co. Runners resolve it correctly, and the activity is the same.
  keepalive:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      SUPABASE_URL: ${{ vars.SUPABASE_URL }}
      SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ vars.SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Keep Supabase active
        run: |
          status="$(curl --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
            --header "apikey: ${SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY}" \
            "${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/profiles?select=id&limit=1")"
          if [ "$status" != '200' ]; then
            printf 'Keepalive returned HTTP %s\n' "$status" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
